title: Justified = God's child; persisting sinner = of the devil—cannot both be true
source_text: XVIII. Praeterea quicunque jam justificatus est, hoc ipso Dei filius est, a Deo adoptatus, & haeres vitae aeternae constitutus: sed quicunque peccato indulget, nec ab eo per veram poenitentiam recessit, ille ex diabolo est. Nam, ut idem Joannes testatur, qui facit peccatum ex diabolo est. Et per hoc manifesti sunt filii Dei, & filii diaboli: Quisquis non dat operam justitiae non est ex Deo. 1 Joh. 3. 8. & 10. Igitur, vel necesse est neminem qui dat operam peccato, & ei mancipatus est, habendum esse pro justificato: vel admittendum, contra manifestam Apostolorum sententiam, aliquem peccatum facere, & justitiae operam non dare, & tamen illum non esse ex diabolo, sed ex Deo; aut, quod veritati non minus repugnat, illum actu simul esse filium Dei, & filium diaboli, vel saltem aliquem justificatum esse qui nondum tamen sit Dei filius.
pass_a_gloss: Further, whoever is already justified is by that very fact God's son, adopted by God, and constituted heir of eternal life: but whoever indulges sin and has not withdrawn from it by true repentance is of the devil. For as the same John testifies, whoever commits sin is of the devil. And by this the children of God and the children of the devil are manifest: whoever does not practice righteousness is not of God (1 John 3:8, 10). Therefore either it is necessary that no one who practices sin and is enslaved to it be held as justified; or one must admit, against the apostles' clear teaching, that someone commits sin and does not practice righteousness and yet is not of the devil but of God; or, what no less conflicts with the truth, that he is actually at once God's son and the devil's son, or at least that someone is justified who is not yet God's son.
pass_b_english: The justified are God's children; unrepentant sinners are of the devil (1 John 3).
Pre-faith justification would make someone God's child and the devil's at once.

lemmas.gloss: son of God and son of the devil

choices.why: Contradiction if justified while still of the devil.
